faq.title: Questions, answered.
faq.lead: Everything you need to know before reaching out. Still curious? Drop us a line — a real engineer will reply.

items.question: What services does Innogenio offer?
items.answer: We're a product engineering studio covering custom software, AI & automation, ERPNext implementation, and data & DevOps. From v1 MVPs to scaling complex platforms, we handle strategy, design, build, and operation end-to-end.

items.question: How much does a project cost?
items.answer: It depends on scope, but we scope transparently. Most engagements start between $25k and $150k+. Tell us your budget range in the form and we'll propose an approach that fits — no surprise invoices, no hidden hand-offs.

items.question: How quickly can we start?
items.answer: Discovery calls happen within a day or two of reaching out. Once scope is agreed, a dedicated team typically kicks off within two to three weeks. Need to move faster? Tell us — we'll do our best to accommodate urgent timelines.

items.question: Do you work with startups as well as enterprises?
items.answer: Both. We act as a technical co-founder for early-stage startups and as a scalable delivery partner for established teams. Our solutions adapt to your goals instead of forcing you to adapt to a fixed process.

items.question: Who owns the code and IP?
items.answer: You do — fully. All source code, designs, and intellectual property belong to you from day one. We build in your repositories with clear documentation so your team can take over at any time.

items.question: How do you handle security and privacy?
items.answer: Security and privacy are designed in from day one, not bolted on. We follow best-practice access control, encryption, and compliance workflows, and we're happy to sign an NDA before any detailed discussion.

items.question: Do you offer support after launch?
items.answer: Yes. We can operate and evolve what we build through ongoing support and DevOps retainers, or hand off cleanly to your in-house team with full documentation and a transition period — your choice.
